purpose: VS-00 source inventory of raw consumers for six existing Lucide glyph names. It compares current app/web callsites and site/src representations with the candidate product semantic registry; it records migration evidence and bounded gaps, not product acceptance or implementation authority.

baseline.source_state: Current worktree has unrelated dirty product edits; source hashes below pin the inspected bytes. No source files were changed by this inventory.
baseline.evidence_mode: Static source inspection only; no browser, screenshot, provider, personal session, or product acceptance.
baseline.path_policy: Repository-relative path:line references; dynamic mappings include both the mapping and render callsite.

scan.app_web_scope: *.mjs and *.js under app/web, excluding vendor/** and product-semantics.generated.mjs; raw entrypoints inspected: icon, action, setAction, flowRow, module icon fields, dynamic glyph returns.
scan.site_scope: All site/src source and registered figure/diagram assets; exact target glyph names checked as literals and SVG href/use references.
scan.notes: The broad app scan also finds CSS class names, activity state/slot identifiers, generated registry text, and the ui-controls allowlist; those are excluded below unless they are an actual glyph argument or mapping return.

consumers.intent: Pending question and approval request rows
consumers.owner: Home presentation; Attention queue and Approval owners supply the facts
consumers.reason: The one mapping covers two request kinds, while chat.object is single-purpose and both queue/request entries are text-reserved or unmapped. Keep the item title, request label, and waiting state in text.

consumers.intent: Open a session candidate as a Chat
consumers.reason: The row title is a conversation and the registry maps message-square only to chat.object. The accessible object name and status remain visible beside the glyph.

consumers.intent: Read an answered or closed question in the stream
consumers.reason: The canonical glyph contract allows message-square for Question, but the current registry reserves it for chat.object and has no question entry. Add an explicit question mapping or remove the decorative type glyph; do not present the question as Chat.

consumers.intent: Answer a pending question in the stream
consumers.reason: The prompt is a Question, not a Chat identity. The existing row precedent is valid only after a distinct question semantic key is admitted; otherwise retain the prompt and Answer control as text and remove the glyph.

consumers.intent: Explain that no Attention items match this project/state
consumers.reason: The empty state already names Attention items. A Chat-only glyph adds a false object cue and no state or action fact.

consumers.intent: Open the persistent Attention assistant
consumers.reason: Attention is text-reserved and distinct from Chat. Keep the visible Attention label and assistant route; the current Chat glyph should not identify the assistant.

consumers.intent: Show retained activity with a scoped period and totals
consumers.reason: This is an explicit recorded Activity view with a period selector and retained-run total, matching the single-purpose registry mapping.

consumers.intent: Group recorded tool actions for one Run
consumers.reason: The group is explicitly titled Activity and is scoped to one Run; it is the canonical recorded-activity use. The group glyph must not be reused for the Run object itself.

consumers.function_or_symbol: toolGlyph → tool row for unrecognized tools
consumers.intent: Give an unknown tool call a neutral type marker
consumers.raw_entrypoint: toolGlyph(name) returns "activity"; flowRow receives glyph: toolGlyph(row.name)
consumers.reason: The current neutral fallback is an Activity glyph on a Tool row. activity.view is reserved for a recorded Activity view; tool.object currently has no glyph. Route through an explicit tool key or remove the row glyph while preserving the tool identifier and state word.

consumers.intent: Identify the Run module in the rail or narrow strip
consumers.owner: Run module owner / Work surface host
consumers.reason: The registry deliberately leaves run.object text-reserved while activity.view is scoped recorded activity. Preserve the Run title and open handler, but do not silently identify the Run object as Activity without an explicit approved variant.

consumers.intent: Open the session context summary
consumers.reason: The label is Chat overview and the callback opens a context summary, not the scoped Activity view. The glyph currently conflates Chat/Run overview with Activity; bind the action to its semantic owner or leave it text-led.

consumers.intent: Identify one recorded Run in the inline summary
consumers.reason: The card title is Run and the registry has no Run glyph. The existing contract uses activity for this card, but the updated registry requires a distinct Run text treatment or an explicitly approved variant.

consumers.intent: Open the latest Run from the session overview
consumers.reason: The row identifies a latest Run, not an Activity interval. Keep the latest status and callback; map the Run object explicitly or remove the Activity glyph.

consumers.intent: Show the target of a resolved local tool Approval
consumers.reason: This branch is a resolved Approval row for a local tool action. activity.view is not the request or tool identity, and approval.request is text-reserved. Keep the exact action words and target; use a dedicated semantic mapping or no glyph.

consumers.surface: New work binding · existing work row
consumers.intent: Continue an existing Matter/work binding for an extension
consumers.reason: The row names existing work and an extension binding, not a configured model connection or MCP service. The older glyph contract explicitly admitted this row, but the registry has no binding semantic; retain only behind an owner-specific mapping.

consumers.intent: Show the producer/status line for an unmounted extension surface
consumers.reason: The title and status identify a producer extension surface, not a model Connection or MCP service. The canonical contract has a plug precedent for this fallback, but the registry needs an extension/producer owner mapping before enforcement.

consumers.intent: Identify the recorded remote target after an Approval decision
consumers.raw_entrypoint: glyph: write ? "square-pen" : remote ? "plug" : "activity"; flowRow(... glyph: display.glyph)
consumers.reason: The target contains an MCP name/server id, so mcp.server is a plausible object identity, but the row is still an Approval receipt with allowed/denied state. The registry must choose which owner is primary; do not let plug imply generic remote Tool or permission.

consumers.intent: Expand/collapse a Project container
consumers.reason: The row is a Project container and the registry maps folder to project.object. The chevron carries expansion state separately.

consumers.intent: Mark a ws_list tool call
consumers.raw_entrypoint: toolGlyph("ws_list") returns "folder"; flowRow receives glyph: toolGlyph(row.name)
consumers.reason: folder is registered for Workspace/Project objects, while this row records a tool action. Preserve the visible ws_list identity and state; use a call-specific tool semantic or no glyph rather than implying a Workspace object.

consumers.intent: Disclose raw fields from a Work packet
consumers.reason: The canonical Review grammar uses folder for Recorded fields, but no recorded-facts semantic is in the current registry. Retain the disclosure title and raw fields; require an explicit packet-facts mapping before treating folder as a registered object glyph.

consumers.intent: Identify the Workspace module
consumers.reason: The module title and data are the session folder binding and files, matching workspace.object. The same mapping is used by the responsive strip.

consumers.intent: Open recorded facts inside a candidate review
consumers.reason: This is a packet-facts disclosure, not a Project or Workspace identity. The existing glyph contract admits folder here, but the registry has no packet-facts key; preserve the text-led disclosure and resolve the semantic owner before keeping the glyph.

consumers.intent: Open the session files/materials dialog
consumers.reason: The row is an action exposing Chat files, not a bare Project container. folder can be retained only through the existing workspace.object or message.reveal mapping with an explicit label; do not let it read as Matter or Chat identity.

consumers.intent: Mark a read-source tool call
consumers.raw_entrypoint: toolGlyph(name) returns "file-text" for ws_read/se_read_source; flowRow receives it
consumers.reason: file-text has no registry entry and the row records a read Tool action, not a generic File object. Keep the tool name and state; add a read-tool mapping or remove the glyph.

consumers.intent: Identify a recorded candidate decision receipt
consumers.raw_entrypoint: flowRow("div", { glyph: "file-text", title: shortRef(candidate_id), meta: decisionWords[...] })
consumers.reason: The canonical contract uses file-text for a decision receipt, but file-text is absent from the current registry and review.open is text-reserved. Preserve candidate id and decision words; route through an explicit receipt/review mapping or no glyph.

consumers.intent: Open a recorded output file by path and hash
consumers.raw_entrypoint: flowRow("button", { glyph: "file-text", title: row.file.path, meta: "Recorded version" }, ...)
consumers.reason: This is a recorded File/Artifact row and the path/hash state is explicit, but file-text has no registry entry. Preserve the separate Recorded version wording; register the file/artifact representation before enforcement.

consumers.intent: Invite the user to choose an item for context
consumers.reason: The empty detail state already explains the next step and has no file object. file-text is unmapped and adds a misleading artifact cue.

consumers.intent: Open a recorded content-version file
consumers.reason: The target is a recorded File, consistent with the older glyph contract, but file-text is not yet a registry mapping. Keep path and Current file action text; add an explicit file representation mapping.

consumers.intent: Open a current session file
consumers.reason: The row names a current file and its size; file-text has no registry entry. Resolve whether the row is workspace.object or message.reveal, then bind a file/read representation without merging current and recorded versions.

consumers.intent: Show the static ws_write result preview
consumers.reason: This is a static preview of a file-write result, not a Settings object. file-text is unmapped; keep it as a text-led specimen or bind it to an approved file/artifact semantic.

consumers.intent: Show current or recorded file path rows
consumers.raw_entrypoint: icon("file-text") in static and openable fileRow branches
consumers.reason: The two fileRow branches are genuine file rows and match the existing file-row precedent, but file-text has no registry entry. Keep current vs recorded state in text and bind the file row to a future file/read key.

consumers.intent: Identify the File module
consumers.raw_entrypoint: fileModule.icon = "file-text"; action(module.icon, module.title, ...) in host strip
consumers.reason: The File module is a stable object precedent, but file-text has no current registry mapping. Preserve the File title and module action while awaiting an explicit file.object representation.

consumers.intent: Identify a rule finding in a candidate review
consumers.raw_entrypoint: flowRow("summary", { glyph: "file-text", title: finding.ruleId, meta: meta.text })
consumers.reason: The existing Review row contract uses file-text, but no file-text registry entry exists and review.open is text-reserved. Keep rule id/status/reason as facts; bind the glyph only through an explicit Review representation.

consumers.intent: Identify one proposed candidate
consumers.reason: The candidate header is a Review object representation in the old contract, but file-text has no registry mapping. Preserve candidate status/lineage and bind through Review only after owner mapping.

consumers.intent: Identify a recorded decision row
consumers.reason: A decision row is Review history, not a generic file. The old glyph contract supplies file-text, but the current registry does not; preserve decision words and candidate id while deferring the glyph mapping.

consumers.intent: List and open recorded Run files
consumers.reason: All three branches are genuine recorded-file rows, but file-text has no registry entry. Preserve path, bytes, reader availability, and the explicit Recorded files / acceptance note; map the file representation separately.

consumers.intent: Open a current workspace file
consumers.reason: The path is the accessible action name and current-file identity, matching the file-row precedent, but file-text lacks a registry entry. Bind through Workspace/file-read semantics without conflating it with recorded Run versions.

consumers.intent: Refresh the workspace read
consumers.reason: This is a named refresh action with a complete accessible name, directly matching the canonical refresh precedent. The current registry has no refresh entry, so later registry enforcement needs a generic action mapping.

consumers.intent: Refresh the extension list
consumers.reason: The label names the read target and the glyph is the canonical named-refresh/retry form. Record the missing registry mapping for refresh actions separately.

consumers.intent: Open the Spark surface
consumers.reason: The glyph is a refresh action while the accessible and visible name is the text-reserved Spark surface. Keep the Spark label and route; do not make a reload glyph stand for Spark identity.

consumers.intent: Refresh the Attention conversation
consumers.reason: This is a named refresh of a conversation read, not the Attention assistant identity. The full label disambiguates the generic action.

consumers.intent: Refresh Run details
consumers.reason: The action names the Run detail read and matches the canonical refresh precedent. It does not represent the Run object.

consumers.intent: Refresh session files
consumers.reason: The full accessible name points to the session-file read and distinguishes refresh from opening a file.

consumers.intent: Retry loading the runtime snapshot
consumers.raw_entrypoint: action("refresh-cw", "Retry loading the runtime", () => void read(), { visible: true })
consumers.reason: This is the explicit retry-reading precedent; visible Retry text and full accessible name carry the action. It must not be confused with starting a Run.

consumers.intent: Refresh the runtime snapshot
consumers.raw_entrypoint: action("refresh-cw", "Refresh the runtime snapshot", () => void read())
consumers.reason: The label names the snapshot read and matches the canonical named-refresh precedent.

consumers.intent: Retry the Run summary read
consumers.reason: The visible Retry text and full name distinguish re-reading a failed summary from re-running work.

consumers.intent: Retry loading the Workspace read
consumers.reason: The shared helper uses a complete Retry label and is the canonical bounded read recovery. It does not confer Workspace or Run capability.

consumers.intent: Refresh workspace files
consumers.reason: The full label names the read and matches the canonical refresh action.

excluded_sources.reason: Defines the static icon allowlist consumed by icon(); it is not a semantic consumer or visible callsite.
Copies registry entries for browser use; not a caller. Its target strings are covered by registry hash/source generation checks.
file-text is a class name on a preformatted file reading, not an icon/glyph argument.
file-text is a class name on a preformatted source reading, not an icon/glyph argument.
activity is used as module, details data-section, tab/slot, or variable text; no glyph is passed at these lines.

Spark and Attention are represented by text, HTML geometry, and registered SVG figures. No target Lucide names, sprite use, or icon() calls occur in site/src; Pages representations are intentionally text/diagram per the registry.
Brand geometry and product-page copy are separate representations; they do not consume the six operational Lucide glyphs.

findings.title: Chat vs Attention
findings.finding: message-square is used for Home pending queue items and global Attention while the registry maps it only to single-purpose chat.object. Home Continue rows are the direct Chat mapping; queue/assistant identity should remain text-led.

findings.title: Spark vs refresh
findings.finding: refresh-cw is correctly used for named read/retry actions, but the Spark navigation button uses it as Spark identity. Keep generic read/retry consumers and remove the identity collision.

findings.title: Approval vs Chat / remote service
findings.finding: Question rows inherit message-square from the older Chat Flow contract without a current question registry entry; resolved remote/local Approval rows return plug/activity. Approval/request text and exact action scope remain primary; registry owner mapping is required before glyph retention.

findings.title: Run vs Activity
findings.finding: Run module, Run summary, latest Run, and Chat overview use activity while the registry maps activity only to scoped recorded activity.view and leaves run.object text-reserved. The Chat Flow Activity group and Home Activity card are legitimate scoped Activity consumers.

findings.title: Unmapped file and refresh glyphs
findings.finding: file-text and refresh-cw have no current registry glyphRef entries. Existing file and named-read contract callsites remain visible migration candidates; generic refresh can keep its established action grammar while registry work adds the missing action/file mappings.
